label: text
text: Their Royal Highnesses the Prince of Wales and the Duke of York were again present in the Gallery of the House of Commons when the debate on the motion authorising the continuance of the Emergency Regulations was resumed.

label: text
text: "A warm discussion ensued over a Labourite objection to the regulation dealing with the protection of property."

label: text
text: Mr. J. Batey (Labourite, Spenny-moor) saw in the regulation an attempt to enable the coal owners to fill the pits with blacklegs. He warned the Government that this would lead to trouble.

label: text
text: Sir Douglas Hogg (Conservative, South Marylebone) in replying said that the suggestion that the people should not be allowed to carry on their business because a body of Trade Unionists had forbidden it was the best justification for this regulation. (Loud Ministerial cheers and angry Labour cries.)

label: text
text: Mr. T. I. Murdy Jones, (Labourite, Pontypridd) hotly said that the Miners' Federation took up Sir Douglas Hogg's challenge. He declared that every miners' member would do his utmost to prevent the mine owners working blackleg labour. The regulations were a scrap of paper as far as the miners were concerned.

label: text
text: Mr. Jack Jones (Labourite, Silvertown) likewise warmly condemned the regulation, saying "Do your damnedest, we are prepared to fight."

label: text
text: The Labourite amendment to the regulation was rejected on a division:—

label: text
text: The Labourites adhered to their policy of moving the rejection of successive emergency clauses, but the amendments were rejected by overwhelming majorities.

label: text
text: Following a short debate on each clause Mr. G. Lansbury (Labourite, Bow and Bromley) moved the deletion of 'the regulation prohibiting acts likely to cause dissatisfaction among His Majesty's Force', Police, Fire Brigades, and the civilian population or to impede the distribution of food and other vital supplies, also the essential transit by locomotion. He provoked irational Ministerial laughter by declaring that already men were being interfered with because they were acting as pickets.

label: text
text: Mr. E. Thurtle (Labourite, Shoreditch) sought the erasure of Regulation 22 empowering the Home Secretary to prohibit meetings and processions where there was reason to apprehend that they would provoke disorder. Mr. Thurtle indulged in dark threats. He said that the West-end was now in the ascendant. When the East was in the ascendant "for every turn of the thumb-screw you give to-day we will give ten"

label: text
text: Sir Douglas Hogg paid a tribute to the exemplary patience and tact of the Police in difficult circumstances. It would be unfair unavoidably to increase their burdens. Nobody could doubt that scenes of disorder could easily be produced by irresponsible processions.

label: text
text: The House signified its agreement by voting for the regulation as follows:—

label: text
text: The same fate befall further cluses, notably that authorising the entry on premises suspected of being used for producing seditious publications, after which the Labourites left the House.

label: text
text: The House confirmed the regulations without a division, only one Labourite being present.

label: text
text: An official communique issued this evening says that abundant food and ample transport are available, but the strikers' pickets are interfering with their distribution. "This aspect will require increasing attention during the next few days, and all attempts to impede the free movement of the public or its food'shall be methodically and firmly repressed." The Navy has rendered prompt and effectual civil assistance at several seaports. No use for the display of armed force has been required.

label: text
text: It adds that the Government's policy to refuse co-operation from the organisers of the general strike should be maintained by all the authorities.

label: text
text: The British "Gazette" states that a considerable amount of business is doing at rates that do not show a panic tendency, though they are naturally higher than on May 3. At present they approximate from 2/6 to 4/2 per £100 for retail shops, according to the nature of the trade, whilst those dealing exclusively in foodstuffs and provisions are quoted at from 4/- to 7/0.

label: text
text: The market insurance against damage by rioters and strikers remains steady.

label: text
text: Disorderly scenes occurred in the Old Kent Road district. A strong body of mounted police and hundreds of foot Policies were engaged in clearing the thoroughfares of dense crowds. Several persons wore injured.

label: text
text: A private car was set on fire, and two fire engines extinguished the flames.

label: text
text: Mr. St. Saklatvala, Communist M.P. for North Battensen, against appeared in Bow Street Police Court. He refused to find two surities and was sentenced to two months' imprisonment.

label: text
text: His counsel told the Magistrate that accused had decided to conduct his own defence.

label: text
text: Saklatvala admitted the fairness and accuracy of the Police report of his speech. He said that his trial was intended for the public good. He did not regard it as a personal prosecution. He considered that in view of the present political outlook he should not be bound over any more than the Premier for the Premier's speech against a section of the community.

label: text
text: The Magistrate declared that no reasonable man could doubt that Saklatvalu's speech was most seditious.

label: text
text: "We Are With You In Your Fight."

label: text
text: At the conclusion of a meeting of the National Security League General Lee Bullard, who held a high command with the United States Army in France, cabled Mr. Baldwin.

label: text
text: "All who believe in democratic and constitutional Government and oppose the destructive policy of Revolutionary Communism in its attempt on the present social order are with you in your fight."

label: text
text: The papers unanimously consider the further decline in French, Belgian, Roumanian and Polish currencies as a result of heavy sales of depreciated moneys on the London Market in order to hold up and keep sterling on par with the dollar.

label: text
text: The “Petit Parisien” states reports compiled by the Finance Ministry distinctly reveal operations which affected in this sense the foreign markets.

label: text
text: M. Raoul Peret has had a long conference with the Governor of the Bank of France and financial personalities. The Council of the Cabinet are to consider the question this morning.

label: text
text: The Cabinet has decided on urgent measures to check the fall in the franc.

label: text
text: The Minister of Finance M. Raoul Peret, after the meeting, said that the fall was undoubtedly due to the influence of foreign stock markets and the British banks seeking to obtain the largest possible quantity of sterling dollars. The fall was not due to the internal situation in France where the position of the Treasury was good and taxes were coming in regularly. The causes of the fall were only temporary.

label: text
text: The single-engined aeroplane in which George Wilkins proposed to make his 1,000-mile Arctic flight had its right wing torn to shreds, the landing gear smashed, and the propeller shattered in striking a hummock of earth on attempting to rise.

label: text
text: This was the second attempt to hop off, the aeroplane's load having been lightened after the first unsuccessful run to field.

label: text
text: The peace negotiation's have been ruptured and hostilities are resuming.

label: text
text: The Riffs are reported to be preparing an attack on the Spanish zone.

label: text
text: The Riffi delegates returned from Abd-el-Krim without the French prisoners they were expected to bring.

label: text
text: Belgian francs in London fluctuated violently. They opened at 165, touched 167 15/16, and reacted to 158½.

label: text
text: The movement is attributed to the resignation of the Finance Minister.

label: text
text: “North east winds, moderate; fair” reads the forecast until noon to-morrow.

label: text
text: This morning's Observatory report states that pressure has decreased considerably over central and N.E. Japan and slightly from the Loochoos to Formosa. It is increased slightly at Shanghai and Haiphong and is nearly stationary from Hongkong to the Philippines. The depression has deepened and is passing north eastward across the Sea of Japan. An anticyclone has formed over China.

label: text
text: S. M. Payne, a building foreman, was fined $5 at the Central Magistracy this morning on a charge of being drunk and behaving in a disorderly manner. at Queen's Road Central yesterday. Pleading to be without money to pay the fine, he was told to go to prison for seven days.

label: text
text: While carrying out a search on the. R.M.S. "Empress of Canada" yesterday morning, after the liner had berthed at the Kowloon Wharf following her arrival from Shanghai, Revenue Officers found 540 rounds of ammunition concealed in the att 'tween decks. It was unclaimed and was handed over to the Water Police.

label: text
text: On inquity from official sources to day, the "China Mail" was informed that the Government had announced no decision regarding the holding of the Sanitary Board election for which Dr. F. M. Graca Ozoria and Dr. S. C. Ho are candidates.

label: text
text: As previously indicated in these columns, there will have to be legislation to get up a list of those who who are qualified to vote but who are exempted from jury service. Possibly, the exempted persons may be asked "to register their names if they wish to vote" but legislation—either by ordinance or by a regulation in the "Gazette"—will be necessary. So far the Government has not announced any decision as to what course will be followed.

label: text
text: A trap set, to catch a Sikh Police constable who had been demanding bribes from a hawker with a threat to have him arrested for obstruction was described by Captain H. F. Bloxham before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning when the man was charged with accepting a bribe and misconduct as a police officer.

label: text
text: Three marked ten-cent pieces changed hands at Ice House Street and when searched before an inspector the coins, together with another 15 cents were found inside the pugarree.

label: text
text: The record produced by Captain Bloxham showed that the man had four year's service and twelve reports against him during this period.

label: text
text: Mr. Leo D'Almada, defending, said that accused had frankly admitted his guilt. He made a strong plea for a fine which would serve as a deterrent.

label: text
text: In imposing sentence of four months' hard labour, His Worship remarked that imprisonment was the only deterrent in cases of this kind.

label: text
text: The exciting early morning chase after an armed robbery committed at No. 35, Connaught Road West on Wednesday had a development at the Central Magistracy this morning when a foki of the firm arrested for alleged collusion with the robbers was brought before the Magistrate.

label: text
text: It will be recalled that one of the bound fokis extricated himself and gave chase to the man who was eventually shot in the neck by a detective at Hillier Street. The other members of the gang escaped with the booty comprising money and jewellery to the value of over $4,000 taken from the ground and first floor.

label: text
text: The captured robber being still in hospital, Det.-Sub-Inspector Lane asked for a formal remand in police custody for three days of the man produced to-day. This was granted.

label: text
text: The assault on an Indian Naval Yard policeman by a Chinese old job coolie who resented interference with his smoking was, witnessed by a bluejacket who came to the rescue.

label: text
text: When the coolie was charged with the offence before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning, Stoker Howe (H.M.S. "Tamar") said that he heard a police whistle being blown and looking in that direction he saw the accused striking the policeman with his fist. The policeman was in difficulties and witness assisted in placing accused under arrest.

label: text
text: Accused denied the charge of assault. He was sent to prison for fourteen days.

label: text
text: A dog, identified as the animal which bit Mr. Chanson a few days ago at Wong-Nel Chong Road, was run over by a motor car and killed. The carcase has been sent to the Bacteriologist.

label: text
text: On the quil vive for developments extending into 'Kwantung province, Canton troops are now reported to be entraining daily (on the Canton-Hankow Railway) as far north as Shlukwan) to strengthen the garrison along the frontiers.

label: text
text: It is yet impossible to say what influence this will have on the situation in Kwangtung. The trend of events in Central China, and along the Yangtse Valley (writes a correspondent) is such that anything may happen.

label: text
text: Most of the troops sent North belong to General Li Chai-sum's army (or army corps). He controls the upper reaches (in the province) of the West River, and the lower stretches of the North River. Passenger traffic on the Railway has been disorganised for at least two days, owing to military transport monopolising the line.

label: text
text: Another chapter has been recorded in the petty warfare waged continually on the 'Canton River' as a result of activities by the boycott pickets.

label: text
text: Native craft have got together crews who describe themselves as the "pugilistic sampana," their business being to convoy fast moving boats with passengers for the steamers bound for Hongkong.

label: text
text: Several fights between the strike breakers and the pickets have taken place recently. "Allies" of the "pugs" are the fish coolies who succeeded in beating off armed pickets and capturing even a number of firearms from the strikers.

label: text
text: On Wednesday night, two such sampans put off from Fongchuen, acting as guard to small passenger boats. When the pickets' motor boats have within range and gave an order to swing to, the sampans answered with a volley. After a running duel, the "pugs" were captured, together with their passengers, who numbered between ten and twenty. These, it is presumed, will have to undergo trial at the strike headquarters.
